verses.english: Numbered Discourses 10.23
3. The Great Chapter
Body

verses.pali: “Atthi, bhikkhave, dhammā kāyena pahātabbā, no vācāya.
verses.english: “Mendicants, there are things that should be given up by the body, not by speech.

verses.pali: Atthi, bhikkhave, dhammā vācāya pahātabbā, no kāyena.
verses.english: There are things that should be given up by speech, not by the body.

verses.pali: Atthi, bhikkhave, dhammā neva kāyena pahātabbā no vācāya, paññāya disvā pahātabbā.
verses.english: There are things that should be given up neither by the body, nor by speech, but by seeing again and again with wisdom.

verses.pali: Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā kāyena pahātabbā, no vācāya?
verses.english: And what are the things that should be given up by the body, not by speech?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akusalaṁ āpanno hoti kiñci desaṁ kāyena.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant has committed a certain unskillful offense by way of body.
After examination, sensible spiritual companions say this to them:

verses.pali: ‘āyasmā kho akusalaṁ āpanno kiñci desaṁ kāyena.
verses.english: ‘Venerable, you’ve committed a certain unskillful offense by way of body.

verses.pali: Sādhu vatāyasmā kāyaduccaritaṁ pahāya kāyasucaritaṁ bhāvetū’ti.
verses.english: Please give up that bad bodily conduct and develop good bodily conduct.’

verses.pali: So anuvicca viññūhi sabrahmacārīhi vuccamāno kāyaduccaritaṁ pahāya kāyasucaritaṁ bhāveti.
verses.english: When spoken to by their sensible spiritual companions they give up that bad bodily conduct and develop good bodily conduct.

verses.pali: Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, dhammā kāyena pahātabbā, no vācāya.
verses.english: These are the things that should be given up by the body, not by speech.

verses.pali: Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā vācāya pahātabbā, no kāyena?
verses.english: And what are the things that should be given up by speech, not by the body?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akusalaṁ āpanno hoti kiñci desaṁ vācāya.
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant has committed a certain unskillful offense by way of speech.
After examination, sensible spiritual companions say this to them:

verses.pali: ‘āyasmā kho akusalaṁ āpanno kiñci desaṁ vācāya.
verses.english: ‘Venerable, you’ve committed a certain unskillful offense by way of speech.

verses.pali: Sādhu vatāyasmā vacīduccaritaṁ pahāya vacīsucaritaṁ bhāvetū’ti.
verses.english: Please give up that bad verbal conduct and develop good verbal conduct.’

verses.pali: So anuvicca viññūhi sabrahmacārīhi vuccamāno vacīduccaritaṁ pahāya vacīsucaritaṁ bhāveti.
verses.english: When spoken to by their sensible spiritual companions they give up that bad verbal conduct and develop good verbal conduct.

verses.pali: Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, dhammā vācāya pahātabbā, no kāyena.
verses.english: These are the things that should be given up by speech, not by the body.

verses.pali: Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā neva kāyena pahātabbā no vācāya, paññāya disvā pahātabbā?
verses.english: And what are the things that should be given up neither by the body, nor by speech, but by seeing again and again with wisdom?

verses.pali: Lobho, bhikkhave, neva kāyena pahātabbo no vācāya, paññāya disvā pahātabbo.
verses.english: Greed …
hate …
delusion …
anger …
acrimony …
disdain …
contempt …

verses.pali: macchariyaṁ, bhikkhave, neva kāyena pahātabbaṁ no vācāya, paññāya disvā pahātabbaṁ.
verses.english: and stinginess are things that should be given up neither by the body, nor by speech, but by seeing again and again with wisdom.

verses.pali: Pāpikā, bhikkhave, issā neva kāyena pahātabbā no vācāya, paññāya disvā pahātabbā.
verses.english: Nasty jealousy should be given up neither by the body, nor by speech, but by seeing again and again with wisdom.
And what is nasty jealousy?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ijjhati gahapatissa vā gahapatiputtassa vā dhanena vā dhaññena vā rajatena vā jātarūpena vā.
verses.english: It’s when a householder or their child is prospering in money, grain, silver, or gold.

verses.pali: Tatrāññatarassa dāsassa vā upavāsassa vā evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: And a bondservant or dependent thinks:

verses.pali: ‘aho vatimassa gahapatissa vā gahapatiputtassa vā na ijjheyya dhanena vā dhaññena vā rajatena vā jātarūpena vā’ti.
verses.english: ‘Oh, may that householder or their child not prosper in money, grain, silver, or gold!’

verses.pali: Samaṇo vā pana brāhmaṇo vā lābhī hoti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṁ.
verses.english: Or an ascetic or brahmin receives robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.

verses.pali: Tatrāññatarassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā evaṁ hoti:
verses.english: And some other ascetic or brahmin thinks:
‘Oh, may that venerable not receive robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick.’
This is called nasty jealousy.

verses.pali: Pāpikā, bhikkhave, icchā neva kāyena pahātabbā no vācāya, paññāya disvā pahātabbā.
verses.english: Corrupt wishes should be given up neither by the body, nor by speech, but by seeing again and again with wisdom.
And what are corrupt wishes?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco assaddho samāno ‘saddhoti maṁ jāneyyun’ti icchati;
verses.english: It’s when a faithless person wishes to be known as faithful.
An unethical person wishes to be known as ethical.
An unlearned person wishes to be known as learned.
A lover of company wishes to be known as secluded.
A lazy person wishes to be known as energetic.
An unmindful person wishes to be known as mindful.
A person without immersion wishes to be known as having immersion.
A witless person wishes to be known as wise.
Someone who has not ended the defilements wishes to be known as having ended the defilements.
These are called corrupt wishes.

verses.pali: Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, dhammā neva kāyena pahātabbā no vācāya, paññāya disvā pahātabbā.
verses.english: Corrupt wishes should be given up neither by the body, nor by speech, but by seeing again and again with wisdom.

verses.pali: Tañce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṁ lobho abhibhuyya iriyati,
verses.english: Suppose that greed masters that mendicant and keeps going.
Or that hate …
delusion …
anger …
acrimony …
disdain …
contempt …
stinginess …
nasty jealousy …
or corrupt wishes master them and keep going.
You should know of them:

verses.pali: ‘nāyamāyasmā tathā pajānāti yathā pajānato lobho na hoti, tathāhimaṁ āyasmantaṁ lobho abhibhuyya iriyati;
verses.english: ‘This venerable does not have the understanding that would eliminate greed, so greed masters them and keeps going.

verses.pali: nāyamāyasmā tathā pajānāti yathā pajānato doso na hoti …
verses.english: They don’t have the understanding that would eliminate hate …
delusion …
anger …
acrimony …
disdain …
contempt …
stinginess …
nasty jealousy …

verses.pali: pāpikā icchā na hoti, tathāhimaṁ āyasmantaṁ pāpikā icchā abhibhuyya iriyatī’ti.
verses.english: or corrupt wishes, so corrupt wishes master them and keep going.’

verses.pali: Tañce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṁ lobho nābhibhuyya iriyati,
verses.english: Suppose that greed does not master that mendicant and keep going.
Or that hate …
delusion …
anger …
acrimony …
disdain …
contempt …
stinginess …
nasty jealousy …
or corrupt wishes don’t master that mendicant and keep going.
You should know of them:

verses.pali: ‘tathā ayamāyasmā pajānāti yathā pajānato lobho na hoti, tathāhimaṁ āyasmantaṁ lobho nābhibhuyya iriyati;
verses.english: ‘This venerable has the understanding that eliminates greed, so greed doesn’t master them and keep going.

verses.pali: tathā ayamāyasmā pajānāti yathā pajānato doso na hoti …
verses.english: They have the understanding that eliminates hate …
delusion …
anger …
acrimony …
disdain …
contempt …
stinginess …
nasty jealousy …

verses.pali: pāpikā icchā na hoti, tathāhimaṁ āyasmantaṁ pāpikā icchā nābhibhuyya iriyatī’”ti.
verses.english: and corrupt wishes, so corrupt wishes don’t master them and keep going.’”
